platforms.name: Mobile App
platforms.detailedDescription: App Fluxo holds significant historical value in my career: it was the first application I built from scratch and my official entry point into mobile development. Built for internal corporate use, it operated as an executive dashboard and operations hub (mini-ERP). Beyond enabling real-time KPI tracking by department (NPS, revenue, contracts), the app solved physical office problems: it managed mezzanine meeting-room scheduling and controlled member shift check-ins via QR code scanning. The authentication architecture was a challenge of its own, integrating OAuth login directly with Podio (the company's management platform) as the Identity Provider, ensuring secure access without the need for a dedicated credentials database.
learnings: Gained hands-on entry into the mobile ecosystem with React Native and Expo (SDK 39), architecting with React Class Components and mastering lifecycle methods like componentDidMount before the Hooks era.

Engineered hardware integration and conditional logic: leveraged expo-barcode-scanner so the QR Code action (Open/Close shift) was intelligently derived from the current state mapped in Redux, eliminating the need for distinct physical codes.
Architected complex global state management with Redux and Redux Thunk to orchestrate asynchronous data, financial metrics, and real-time team operational status.
Prioritized UX and micro-interactions: implemented real-time Regex validation on login, strategic auto-focus via the native keyboard, and conditional color algorithms for team health metrics.
Implemented complex UI components, such as react-native-calendars for managing mezzanine scheduling conflicts, using native date-pickers and manual date formatting.

Engineered a standardized global error-handling system (ShowError) for API failures or missing hardware permissions, and enforced rigorous layout constants for fluid responsiveness across screen sizes.
